artifacts.notes: 2,007 PDF pages carrying a Google Books text layer of usable quality; the Sundays after Pentecost begin near PDF page 1115. No English oration text is vendored from it. Two reasons: the exact bytes have an unresolved rights status, so a verbatim extract could not be tracked, and the Mass formularies are set in two columns whose language sides alternate from element to element, so a mechanical extraction cannot be trusted to separate the English from the Latin without a page-image check of every formulary. Existing repository research quotes short passages from it after visual collation of individual pages; that remains the safe use.
artifacts.rights_basis: The 1925 printing is in the public domain in the United States by publication date. The exact bytes registered here are a Google Books digitisation republished by Corpus Christi Watershed; the audit located no statement establishing redistribution rights for this exact scanned and text-layered PDF, and neither the age of the book nor its public availability establishes rights in the digitisation. Triptych records the exact remote bytes and retains no payload.

edition.authority: Imprimatur of Theodorus, Abbot of the monastery of Saint André de Zevenkerken, 21 March 1924; Nihil obstat William Busch; Imprimatur Austin Dowling, Archbishop of Saint Paul, 13 May 1925
edition.notes: This 1925 edition is already in use elsewhere in the repository as a historical English prayer and oration witness. It is a pre-1955 book: its Holy Week, octaves, vigils, and second and third orations are those of the Divino afflatu discipline, not of 1962. Its running commentary and rubrical explanations are the editor's, not liturgical text.
edition.publication: Lophem near Bruges, Belgium: Liturgical Apostolate, St. Andrew's Abbey; St. Paul, Minnesota: The E. M. Lohmann Co., 385 St. Peter Street, 1925
edition.title: Daily Missal with Vespers for Sundays and Feasts

work.author: Gaspar Lefebvre, O.S.B., of the Abbey of Saint André
work.description: Dom Gaspar Lefebvre's liturgical hand missal, the ancestor of the later Saint Andrew Daily Missal, giving the Ordinary, the temporal and sanctoral Masses, and Vespers of Sundays and feasts in facing Latin and English with liturgical commentary. In the Mass formularies the Latin and English are set in two columns whose sides alternate, so a column is not reliably one language. Later Saint Andrew editions of 1940, 1945, 1949, 1953, and 1962 are separate expressions whose United States copyright status was not established here and which are not registered.
work.title: Daily Missal with Vespers for Sundays and Feasts
